chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, and from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Aslam, from Ibrahim ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from Aban ibn Taghlib, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom. A man marries a woman for Mut'ah (temporary marriage), and marries her for a month. Then it occurs in his heart, and he wishes that his stipulation be more than a month. So, is it permissible for him to increase her in her recompense (dowry) and increase in the days before the days he stipulated for her expire?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'No. Two stipulations are not allowed in one stipulation.' I said: 'What should he do?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should give charity to her with whatever remains of the days, then he resumes with a new stipulation.'

key_terms.شَرْطٌ: Stipulation/condition (referring to the duration and dowry)

ai.seo_question: How to extend the duration of temporary marriage (Mut'ah) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic principle of 'two conditions in one condition' (shartan fi shart) within Shia temporary marriage (Mut'ah), prohibiting the mere extension of an existing contract's duration. Instead, it mandates a distinct legal procedure: the husband must first settle the remaining dowry (sadaq) for the unexpired days of the initial contract and then initiate a completely new contract for the extended period. This ensures contractual clarity and prevents ambiguity in the rights and obligations of both parties.
